identity.name: Laurent Ferrier Galet Classic Micro-Rotor

case.material: stainless steel (also in white and rose gold)

identity.one_liner: The Galet Classic Micro-Rotor is the watch that established Laurent Ferrier as the most-cited independent watchmaker of the 2010s — a hand-finished in-house micro-rotor movement in a 40mm pebble-shaped case.

narrative.story: Laurent Ferrier founded his eponymous brand in 2010, after a 37-year career at Patek Philippe (where he was technical director under the Stern family). The Galet Classic Micro-Rotor was his debut watch: a 40mm pebble-shaped case in stainless steel, a hand-finished in-house micro-rotor movement with an 80-hour reserve, and the most-cited finishing standard in the independent watchmaking world. Ferrier produces roughly 200 watches per year across all his lines. The Galet Classic Micro-Rotor is the most-cited of the brand's output and the most-cited example of a watch that came from a former Patek Philippe director.
narrative.collector_notes: The LF 230.01 movement is decorated with "Côtes Rompues" (broken waves) perlage — a finish that takes a master watchmaker roughly 8 hours per movement. The micro-rotor is in 22k gold. The case is named "Galet" (pebble) for its rounded, polished silhouette. Production is roughly 50 pieces per year in steel.
